evals.prompt: Give me a Python OpenAI SDK example for my inventory app to call the AI Station coder model, including how to create a restricted key.
evals.expected_output: A least-privilege project key workflow and SDK example using LiteLLM :4000/v1 with an environment key.
expectations: Loads the key from an environment variable
Does not use internal ports or a GGUF path

evals.prompt: Set up OpenCode from Windows for all of my local AI Station coding models and prove it can actually edit and test code.
evals.expected_output: Uses the WSL-native non-root runtime, doctor and acceptance, keeps one provider, and distinguishes DeepSeek non-tool capability.
expectations: Uses ai opencode configure rather than hand-editing the key
Runs OpenCode inside WSL as the non-root developer user
Uses doctor and the edit-and-test acceptance harness
Keeps one ai-station provider and all picker models visible
Does not claim DeepSeek tool support

evals.prompt: Three internal apps need different AI Station models and limits. Should they share the LiteLLM master key?
evals.expected_output: Rejects master-key sharing and recommends isolated project virtual keys, allowlists, limits, and independent revocation.
expectations: Uses one virtual key per app
Uses model allowlists and rate/token limits
Mentions independent revocation and secret redaction
